problem:
Title: Characteristic of Ordered Integral Domain is Zero

Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an [[Definition:Ordered Integral Domain|ordered integral domain]] whose [[Definition:Ring Zero|zero]] is $0_D$ and whose [[Definition:Unity of Ring|unity]] is $1_D$.

Let $\Char D$ be the [[Definition:Characteristic of Ring|characteristic of $D$]].

Then $\Char D = 0$.

Let $g: \Z \to D$ be the [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] defined as:
:$\forall n \in \Z: \map g n = n \cdot 1_D$
where $n \cdot 1_D$ is defined as the [[Definition:Power of Element|$n$th power of $1_D$]].

Then $g$ is the only [[Definition:Ring Monomorphism|monomorphism]] from the [[Definition:Ordered Ring|ordered ring]] $\Z$ onto the [[Definition:Ordered Ring|ordered ring]] $D$.
proof_numbered:
0001 | By [[Properties of Ordered Ring]] $(5)$:
0002 | :$\forall n \in \Z_{>0}: n \cdot 1_D > 0$
0003 | 
0004 | Thus:
0005 | :$\forall p > 0: \Char D \ne p$
0006 | 
0007 | Hence:
0008 | :$\Char D = 0$
0009 | 
0010 | and so $g$ is a [[Definition:Ring Monomorphism|monomorphism]] from $\Z$ into $D$.
0011 | 
0012 | Also, if $m < p$, then $p - m \in \Z_+$, so:
0013 | :$p \cdot 1_D - m \cdot 1_D > 0_D$
0014 | 
0015 | Hence:
0016 | :$\map g m < \map g p$
0017 | 
0018 | Thus by [[Monomorphism from Total Ordering]], $g$ is a [[Definition:Ring Monomorphism|monomorphism]] from $\Z$ into $D$.
0019 | {{qed}}
